questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The interviewer asked Ashok, "Why did you leave that job last month?"

options.text: The interviewer asked Ashok why you have left that job the previous month.
The interviewer asked Ashok that why did he leave that job the previous month.
The interviewer asked Ashok that why he leave that job the last month.
The interviewer asked Ashok why he had left that job the previous month.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 4.**
 
• Given active sentence is in interrogative form therefore interrogative will be changed to an assertive sentence. To change the sentence into an indirect sentence. Simple past will be changed to past perfect tense, 'last month' will be changed to 'previous month'. 
 
• **Therefore, all these conditions are satisfied only in option 4.**

questions.question:

__
 
• The error lies in the usage of the **indefinite article 'a__**' with an **__uncountable__ noun** __**'weather**__**'.**

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

They will complete the painting in a week's time.

options.text: The painting will be completed in a week's time.
The painting is completed in a week's time.
The painting was completed in a week's time.
The painting had been completed in a week's time.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1. **
 
• In active voice, the subject performs the action denoted by the verb.
 
• On the other hand, a sentence is in the passive voice when the subject of the sentence is acted upon by the verb.
 
• When changing from active voice to passive, we do not change the tense of the given sentence.
 
• **Except Option 1 all other options are in different tense. Therefore option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(140, 85, 115)
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

(140, 85, 115) → 140 ÷ 5 = 28 and 115 ÷ 5 = 23; (28 + 23) ÷ 3 = 51 ÷ 3 = 17 × 5 = 85 the middle term.

Similary, 

(115, 65, 80) → 115 ÷ 5 = 23 and 80 ÷ 5 = 16; (23 + 16) ÷ 3 = 39 ÷ 3 = 13 and 13 × 5 = 65 the middle term.

Hence, the correct answer is (115, 65, 80)

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some autos are cycles.

All cycles are trucks.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some trucks are autos.

II. Some trucks are cycles.

III. Some cycles are autos.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is given below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b318a82f7997bd0a993224f3866d58010595866c89fda334652d371e1ceee93.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some trucks are autos → True (Those autos which are cycles are trucks.)

II. Some trucks are cycles → True (all cycles are trucks).

III. Some cycles are autos → True (some autos are cycles.)

Hence, the correct answer is 'all conclusions follow'.

questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

612 ÷ 36 – 12 × 88 + 208 = 324
questions.solution:
Given equation: 612 ÷ 36 – 12 × 88 + 208

After Interchanging × and –

612 ÷ 36 × 12 - 88 + 208

= 17 × 12 - 88 + 208 

= 204 – 88 + 208

= 412 – 88

= 324

Hence, the correct answer is × and –.

questions.question: A total sum of Rs. 209 is distributed among three friends A, B and C in such a way that A gets six times rupees than B, C gets 4 times rupees than B. How many rupees does A get?
questions.solution:
Given that:

A + B + C = 209 ...... (i)

A = 6B ......(ii)

C = 4B .......(iii)

From (i), (ii) and (iii),

6B + B + 4B = 209

⇒11B = 209

⇒ B = 209 ÷ 11

⇒ B = 19

Therefore, A = 6 × 19 = 114

Hence, A gers 114 rupees.

questions.question:

questions.question: If a³ – b³ = 899 and a – b = 31, then (a – b)² + 3ab is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

⇒ a3 - b3 = 899

⇒ a - b = 31

**Formula used:**

(a - b)² = a² + b² - 2ab

a3 - b3 = (a - b) (a2 + b2 + ab)

**Calculation:**

⇒ a³ - b³ = (a - b) × (a² + b² + ab)

⇒ a³ - b³ = (a - b) × (a² + b² + ab + 2ab - 2ab)

⇒ a³ - b³ = (a - b) × ((a² + b² - 2ab) + 3ab)

⇒ a³ - b³ = (a - b) × ((a - b)² + 3ab)

Putting the values,

⇒ (a³ - b³) / (a - b) = (a - b)² + 3ab

⇒ 899/31 = (a - b)² + 3ab

⇒ (a - b)² + 3ab = 29

**∴ The correct answer is 29.**

questions.question: If x⁴ + x⁻⁴ = 194, (x > 0), then the value of (2x – 4)² is
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x4 + x-4 = 194

**Formula used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculation:**

x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 194 ----(1)

⇒ (x² + 1/x²)² – 2 = 194

⇒ (x² + 1/x²)² = 194 + 2

⇒ x² + 1/x² = √196

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 14 ----(2)

⇒ (x + 1/x)² – 2 = 14

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 14 + 2

⇒ (x + 1/x) = √16

⇒ x + 1/x = 4

⇒ x² + 1 = 4x

⇒ x² – 4x = –1 ----(3)

We have to find the value of (2x – 4)²

4 (x – 2)²

⇒ 4 (x² – 4x + 4)

⇒ 4 (–1 + 4), from (3)

⇒ 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__****Concept used:**

⇒ x4 + 1/x4 = p

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = √{p + 2} 

**Calculation:**

According to the question:

⇒ x4 + x-4 = 194

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = √{194 + 2}

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 14

Now, 

⇒ x + 1/x = √{14 + 2}

⇒ x + 1/x = √16 = 4

⇒ x² + 1 = 4x

⇒ x2 + 4x = - 1 ------(1)

So, (2x – 4)2 = (2)² (x - 2)²

⇒ 4 (x – 2)2

⇒ 4 (x2 – 4x + 4)

⇒ 4 (–1 + 4), from (1)

⇒ 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

questions.question: A dealer buys an article marked at Rs. 30000 with two successive discounts of 20% and 5%. He spends Rs. 1200 on repairs and sells it for Rs. 30000, what is his profit/loss percent?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

C.P of article = marked price × 80% × 95%

So, C.P of article = 30000 × 4/5 × 19/20 = 22800

Additional expenditure = 1200 

So, total C.P of article = 22800 + 1200 = 24000

Given that S.P of article = 30000

So, gain = 30000 – 24000 = 6000

Gain% = (gain /C.P) × 100

Gain% = (6000/24000) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

questions.question: The average age of fifteen person is 32 years. If two more persons are added then the average is increased by 3 years. The new person have an age difference of 9 years between them. The age (in years) of the younger among the new persons is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average age of 15 person is 32 years.

**Formula used: **

Average age = sum of ages of all persons/number of persons

**Calculation:**

Sum of ages of 15 persons = average age × 15

Sum of ages of 15 persons = 32 × 15 = 480

Let the ages of two persons are x and y

According to question,

Average age of 17 persons = 32 + 3 = 35

So, the sum of ages of 17 persons = 17 × 35 = 595

According to the question:

Sum of ages of 15 person + x + y = sum of ages of 17 persons 

⇒ 480 + x + y = 595

⇒ x + y = 595 – 480

⇒ x + y = 115 ----(1)

It is given that their age difference is 9 years 

⇒ x – y = 9 ----(2)

On subtracting (2) from (1) we get

⇒ y = 53

**∴ The age of younger person = 53 years**

questions.question: In ΔABC, ∠A = 52°. Its side AB and AC are produced to the points D and E respectively. If the bisectors of the ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at point O, then ∠BOC is equal to:

⇒ ∠BOC = 90° - ∠A/2

⇒ ∠BOC = 90° - (52°/2)

⇒ ∠BOC = 90° - 26°

⇒ ∠BOC = 64°

**∴ The correct answer is 64°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

∠A = 52°

**Calculation:**

∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

52° + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

∠B + ∠C = 128°

Let ∠B = x° , ∠C = y°

Now, 

AB is extended to D, 

∠ABD = 180°

∠ABD = ∠ABC + ∠DBC = 180°

x + ∠DBC = 180° 

∠DBC = (180° - x)

Similarly, 

∠ECB = (180° - y)

Now,

As per the triangle Law,

frac{{angle ECB}}{2} + frac{{angle DBC}}{2} + angle O = {180^ circ }

frac{{{{180}^ circ } - x}}{2} + frac{{{{180}^ circ } - y}}{2} + angle O = {180^ circ }

{180^ circ } - (x)/(2) - (y)/(2) + angle O = {180^ circ }

angle O = frac{{x + y}}{2} = frac{{{{128}^ circ }}}{2} = {64^ circ }

∴ The correct answer is 64°.

questions.question: In economics, IPO stands for ______.
questions.solution:

• It could be a new, young company or an old company which decides to be listed on an exchange and hence goes public.
 
• Companies can raise equity capital with the help of an IPO by issuing new shares to the public or the existing shareholders can sell their shares to the public without raising any fresh capital.
 
• The company which offers its shares, known as an** 'issuer'.**

questions.question: Which article of the Constitution of India provisions for reservations of seats for scheduled castes and scheduled tribes in the House of People?

questions.question: Who was the first woman to become the governor of an Indian state?
questions.solution:

questions.question: In which year was the Chicago (USA) Conference of World Religions held that included Swami Vivekananda's talk on religion as one of its highlights?
questions.solution:

• The World Congress of Religions marks the first formal gathering of representatives of Eastern and Western spiritual traditions.
 
• **Swami Vivekananda** mesmerized the 5,000 assembled delegates, greeting them with the words, **“Sisters and brothers of America!” **
 
• This speech, which introduced** Hinduism to America** is memorized by school children in India to this day.
 
• Swami Vivekananda became one of the most forceful and popular speakers in spite of the fact that he had never before addressed an audience in public.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The first woman to win a Nobel Prize was **Marie Curie**__, who won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 with her husband, Pierre Curie, and Henri Becquerel.
 
• Together with her husband, Pierre, she discovered radium, an element widely used for treating cancer and studied uranium and other radioactive substances
 
• In 1911, she won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the isolation of radium.
 
• Curie is also the only woman to have won multiple Nobel Prizes.

questions.question: For economists, ________ refers to the amount of a product or service that people are both willing and able to buy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. __Demand.__**

 
• **Demand **in economics is defined as consumers' willingness and ability to consume a given good.
 
• **Supply** in economics is defined as the total amount of a specific good or service that is available to consumers.
 
• The** law of demand** says that at higher prices, buyers will demand less of an economic good.
 
• The** law of supply** says that at higher prices, sellers will supply more of an economic good.

questions.question: ________ is the smallest unit of data in a computer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. __Bit.__**

__
 
• A** bit__ **is a binary digit and it is the **smallest** unit of data on a computer.
 
• A** **__**bit**__ can hold only one of two values:** 0 or 1.**
 
• Bits are usually assembled into a group of eight to form a byte.
 
• 1 Kilobyte = 1024 Bytes.
 
• 1 Megabyte = 1024 Kilobytes.
 
• 1 Gigabyte = 1024 Megabytes.
 
• 1 Terabyte = 1024 Gigabytes.
